Senses.PreferredTarget: take up an old case for comment
AlternateTargets: raise and comment on an old case
Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses across six source files and five independent works cover enumeration, reading, counting, collection title, contents headings, and a demonstrated section.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古來有拈古、頌古、徵古、代古、別古
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wansong Xingxiu's Evaluations of Hongzhi Zhengjue's Old Cases (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚拈古請益錄): Wansong Xingxiu is the exact speaker in this continuous evaluation and enumerates old-case raising, verse, probing, substitution, and alternative responses. Shakyamuni Buddha, Yangshan Huiji, and Fayan Wenyi are quoted or discussed within Wansong's evaluation, while Hongzhi Zhengjue is the old-case author being commented upon. The Fayan header is not the speaker of this genre list.

Collected Anthology of Raising Old Cases in the Zen Lineage (宗門拈古彙集), preface by compiler Jingfu: the impersonal document heading names the preface to the collection of comments on old cases; it is not a speech turn.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword is embedded in the cb:mulu and head title 宗門拈古彙集序 before the preface prose begins; it has no speech predicate or personal grammatical subject.

Occurrences.Kwic: 余閱雪竇拈古至百丈再叅馬祖因
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of State Preceptor Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), in Yulin Tongxiu's later raising: Zhang Shangying, called Zhang Wujin (張無盡), is the exact first-person speaker who says that he was reading Xuedou Chongxian's comments on old cases. Xuedou is the author discussed, not the speaker of the quoted line.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 余閱 makes the quoted speaker the first-person subject who says he was reading Xuedou's old-case comments; Yulin Tongxiu introduces and raises Zhang's statement in his own record.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of State Preceptor Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄), instruction to Huiji Zhou: Yulin Tongxiu says that after Huiji returned to his hall office he presented more than ten old-case comments. Huiji is the person described as presenting them; Yulin is the exact utterer of the written headword.

Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄), impersonal table-of-contents scene: the fascicle-three heading labels old-case comments and verse comments; it is document structure, not a saying by Zhongfeng Mingben.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 卷第三拈古頌古 is a table-of-contents label naming the contents of fascicle three; it is not a personal utterance or action.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), impersonal table-of-contents scene: the fascicle-eighteen heading labels the lower old-case-comment section and upper verse-comment section. Yuanwu Keqin owns the record but does not utter the heading.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The headword occurs between 卷第十八 and paired section labels; the line has no speech marker or human grammatical subject.

Senses.Explanation: Chan records use this label for a specific prose operation: taking up a preserved old case so a later commentator can place a fresh response beside it. Wansong Xingxiu enumerates it alongside versifying, probing, substituting, and giving an alternative to an old case, which marks it as a distinct commentarial operation. Zhang Shangying says he was reading Xuedou’s old-case comments, and Yulin Tongxiu counts more than ten pieces presented by a student. Book, fascicle, and section headings label collections or divisions of these comments. Tiyin Yuanxiu’s section then demonstrates the form by raising Baizhang’s great-peak case before marking Tiyin’s prose comment. Act, resulting piece, and editorial section are grammatical views of the same operation.
